verdict.rationale: Caveman's own docs describe a first-party agent ('Caveman, our own agent') that takes delegated tasks. You tell it what you want done, and it starts chats, answers their questions, reports back, and proceeds autonomously when you don't respond. Cloud computers let agents verify their own work while you watch, take over and hand back. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the built-in agent's delegation scope and limits (the evidence is short marketing-page claims), independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent (community discussion covers only the response-compression skill).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Claude Agent, Codex, Cursor and Caveman, our own agent, work side by side in tabs and splits.
Tell it what you want done. It starts the chats, answers their questions, reports back, and goes ahead on its own when you don't answer in time.
On a Cloud computer an agent drives a Linux desktop and a browser to check its own work. Watch it live, take over, hand back.
